source: You got Lincoln's envelope.
You got the missing hand.
Lincoln claims he didn't see anything.
Lincoln claims the teens are behind the theft.
Lincoln claims the woman up the street is behind the theft.
You got the missing hand.
You got a pack of cigarettes.
You got a pack of cigarettes.
A picture? Naw, I don't look so good in pictures.
Come on, man. Anything I can do to change your mind?

Nah-uh. That's a City clock. Any work on that has to go through the proper channels. Whole process usually takes two to three months. But once it does? Ka-ching. I ain't clever, but not dumb enough to fix it for free.
Figures.
Wow. Well, thanks for the help.
Yeah, I don't think I'd like that. I'm not really photogenic.
Is there anything I can do to change your mind?

It's a letter I stole from the building manager's mailbox. I thought it was going to be someone complaining about me, but it turned out to be a Winter Solstice card. So I'm going to need you to destroy it.
Why do you have to destroy it?
Why don't you just put the card back without the envelope?

I, uh...spilled some coffee on it. And it's got my paw prints all over it. I'm the only one of my Kind in the building so they'll know it's me. Look, I know it was wrong, I just... I don't want to go away for mail tampering.
Well, neither do I!
I'll take care of it. [Leave]
Alright, listen. Let's make a deal: I'll take whatever photo you want, so long as we keep this between us. If word of this gets out, I'll be ruined. Work's already hard to come by as it is.
You got yourself a deal.
Hmm. I'd rather not be involved in something this sordid, but if you insist...

Huh. Well, that's only because it would be wrong to waste it. I mean, it's not the gift certificate's fault that I thought it was a complaint letter. Look, I made a stupid mistake. How about I donate it to charity. Yeah! That's what I'll do. I'll donate it to charity!
I don't believe you.
What charity?
I don't know, kid. I don't even know if charities accept gift certificates. How about this, instead: I'll take whatever silly photo you want, so long as you keep this between us.
That's all you needed to say.
Hmm. I'd rather not get involved in something this sordid, but if you insist...
Y-you did? Thanks, kiddo. I appreciate it. Just let me know if you ever have a clock that needs fixing, or something.
No problem. Can I ask you something else, by the way?
Sure, man. I'll see you later. [Leave]
Ah, one of the tenants was getting up in my face about the nose of my repairs waking him up and it got kind of...heated.
What happened?
What time were you working on it?
Now don't be doing anything weird with that, alright?
Of course not. Later.
We'll see.
Hey, I'm serious!
Relax. I'm a good boy. [Leave]
So am I.  [Wink]
You're a good kid. Unlike those greasy geezers. Here you go. It should slot right in, no problem.
Appreciate it.
Don't talk shit about geezers, man. The City is theirs as much as it is ours. Later.
You better be kidding!
I guess time will tell. [Leave]
Totally had you, didn't I?
Heh. You're a real rascal, kid.
[Scamper away]
Alright, fine. It was cash. Fifty dollars. You happy? Hardly anything. And considering how much that building manager's been screwing me on supplies, that barely makes us even.
I doubt she'd see it that way.
Was it really only fifty dollars?
Sure, kid. Hah - can't wait to tell my wife I now qualify as 'beautiful'. She's going to flip her lid!
Happy I could help. [Leave]
Please, just hurry up and take the photo.
[Take picture]
Ah, c'mon, kid. I would have told you if I knew something.
Yeah, yeah. [Leave]
I'm just playing with you man. Let's talk about something else.
9 AM. Maybe a little after.
Then what happened?
9 AM is pretty early.
It is if you're a deadbeat. Not that I called him that!
What did you call him?
Sounds like you were just doing your job.
That's not a polite question.
My thoughts exactly.
Exactly. And now it's time for you to make amends.
Winter Solstice. Folks around here really eat that shit up.
And you don't?
I'm more interested in the type of mask you're wearing...
Alright, alright. Here, take it. It should be an easy fix. Just apply a little pressure and you'll be right as rain.
Appreciate it.
Don't talk shit about geezers, man. The City is theirs as much as it is ours. Later.
It's nice. Too nice.
Something lurking beneath the surface?
How can something be "too nice"?
Nothing that sinister. I’m sure it's true of some people around here, but you can find that anywhere. I'm just always afraid of breaking something. Or offending someone.
Sounds miserable.
Why don't you work somewhere else?

You ever hold something really expensive in your hand and start sweating because you’re afraid you might break it? It’s like that, except around here it’s the expensive thing that’s holding you. And it doesn’t give a shit if you break.
Why don't you work somewhere else?
Sounds miserable.
I think it's just an excuse to play dress up and stay home. But the residents tend to give you the side-eye if you don't participate, so that's why I got one.
Path of least resistance, huh?
What made you go for the raccoon?
Oh, uh, yeah. It's uh, I mean, I'm not trying to be mean-spirited here. If anything it's a celebration of your Kind.
And exactly how are you celebrating 'my Kind'?
Doesn't feel like a celebration to me.
Just picking it, you know? I mean, they had all kinds of...'Kind' down at the costume shop. Doesn't it say something that this is the one I choose?
Maybe you picked it because you thought it was funny. A 'joke'.
Depends why you picked it.
Just kind of curious why you picked Raccoon. No real reason?
Something like that. Also, it's harder for the residents to complain about you when you're wearing a disguise.
Interesting. Let's talk a bit more about you.
If you say so. See you later, man.
No joke! No joke! I love raccoons. Raccoons are the coolest. My son's friends with a raccoon and I think that's great! Better than great!
Great? What, better than everyone else?
Hah! Man, you are too easy!
Wait. Were you messing with me?
You totally bought it!
[Continue laughing]
Come on, kid. I was actually worried I offended you.
Oh, you did.
Nah man. I'm jealous I don't have a mask of your Kind.
Hmmm. Well, there is one thing you could do. Here, this envelope - I need you to destroy this for me.
[Take envelope] What is it and why?
Why I picked it? I don't know... I guess it just looked the most fun. I like the colours.
I like your colours too.
I'm more than just my colours, man.
Please don't tell her. I'll do anything. How about this? I'll take whatever photo you want, so long as you keep this between us. If word of this gets out, I'll be ruined.
That's all you needed to say, man.
Hmm. I'd rather not be involved in something this sordid, but if you insist...
...Alright, alright. Maybe next year, I could wear a mask of my own Kind. Yeah, no one would suspect it's me under something like that!
There you go. Let's talk a bit more about you, though.
I'm just messing with you, my man. Let's talk about something else.
Just having a bit of fun. Talk to you later, man. [Leave]
I think they still have some in stock at some places. It's not really a hot-seller, unfortunately.
Let's talk a bit more about the man behind the mask, shall we?
Alright, enough about you. Let's talk about something else.
That sucks, man. Maybe next year. [Leave]

Nothing! I told him it wouldn’t take much longer and to take a walk. And the way I meant that was that if the noise bothered him so much, he should get some fresh air until I'm done. But he says I had a "tone" and the "tone" was me telling him to "get lost".
(INVESTIGATIVE) You sure that's the way you meant it?
Sounds like a simple misunderstanding.
Sounds like a real jerk.
I figured they'd think I was repairing it. And it seemed worth the risk. The City pays me a mint whenever that thing breaks down. Problem is, it rarely does.
Just hand over the part, man.
That's really disappointing, man.
Yeah, but if you're the building manager who are you gonna side with? The guy you're paying or the guy who's paying you?
Well, it's all taken care of now, so hopefully that's the end of it.
Seems like you don't have to worry about that. At least for the time being.
I mean, yeah. Like I said, it got kind of heated. And his "tone" had a lot of "tone" too. So, uh...maybe I matched his?
Well, it's all taken care of now, so hopefully that's the end of it.
Not enough for him to write a complaint though.
Really appreciate you doing that, kid. You're a real class act.
No problem. Let's talk a bit more about you, though.
Happy to help. Let's talk about something else, though.
No problem, brother. [Leave]

I stole it from the building manager's mailbox. I saw a tenant I had an argument with drop it off and figured it was going to be a letter of complaint. Turns out it was just a Winter Solstice card. Now I have to destroy this thing, but I can't risk getting caught.
(INVESTIGATIVE) Was there money inside that card?
Why do you need to destroy it?
Why don't you just put the card back without it's envelope?
This is really suspicious.
Yeah. Guess I let my paranoia get the best of me. Embarrassing. You'll get rid of that letter for me, won't you?
We'll see. I want to know a bit more about you first, though.
Still mulling that one over. Let's change the subject.
I'll get back to you on that. [Leave]
The work itself's nothing to sneeze at. I love coming in, seeing something busted to shit and getting to turn it into something good as new. You feel useful. Important.
Sounds wonderful.
What don't you like?
Only downside is that it's not really steady work. You have to save your money when it's going well. And learn how to scare up customers when it's not.
How's business right now?
Why don't you just get a full time position that's more steady?

There's always tons of repairs in winter and summer. But now that we've hit the Soltice, things are really going to start drying up in a couple months. And that's something I'm going to have to plan for.
Hmm. Let's talk a bit more about you.
Right. Let's talk about something else.
Good luck with that, man. [Leave]
I don't know, kid. Why don’t you just become a big shot photographer?
Point taken.
That's the plan.
I don't mean to be rude. It's just that those gigs are really hard to come by. And the ones that do always like to take advantage.
Sounds about right. Let's talk a bit more about you.
Tough racket. Let's talk about something else.
Well, I hope things pick up for you, man. [Leave]
Heh. Hope you're right, kid. It'd be nice to see a win for us little guys.
Thanks, man. Let's talk a bit more about you.
Appreciate that. Let's talk about something else, though.
Take it easy. [Leave]
What do you want to know?
What kind of complaint were you expecting in that envelope?
I noticed you have a mask...
What's your take on this neighbourhood?
What's it like being a mechanic?
You live around here?
You trying to be funny, kid? I can't even afford to buy lunch around here! Nah, I'm in a sixth floor walkup just off Granville. At least it's three bedrooms, though.
Sounds nice.
Six floors?
It would be if there were only two of us. Unfortunately it's me,  my wife, her parents, and our two youngest.
Yikes. Tell me a bit more about yourself.
That sounds like a lot. Let's change the subject.
Yeesh. Good luck with all that. [Leave]
Heh. Yeah, you should see the calves on my youngest. Four years old and you can already tell she's going to be an athlete.
Heh. Tell me a bit more about yourself.
Always a silver lining. Let's talk about something else, though.
Huh. I'll catch you later. [Leave]
What kind of work do you do?
Oh. I'm student. Photography.
I'm an artist. Photography, mostly.
Well, if you want that picture, you're the one who's going to have to get rid of it. Any other questions?
Nah, I'm good. [Leave]
Yeah, let's talk about something else.

I like doing quality work, kid. And this is one of the few areas where people are willing to pay for that.  You should see the rush jobs the slumlords on the West End try to force on you. Shortcuts like those always backfire, I don't want that on my head.
Couldn't you just report them to the City? Force them to do the right thing?
Wouldn't it be better to have someone skilled like you?
I'm really sorry about that business with the clock, kid. I guess I just let my desperation get the best of me. Won't happen again.
It's fine. I fixed it.
It's okay. You're just doing what you can to get by.
Sure. See ya. [Leave]
I want to talk to you about something.
Skill has nothing to do with it. Good work take time. And most places pay by the job, not by the time.
Hmm. Right. Let's talk a bit more about you.
Makes sense. Why don't we talk about something else?
Gotcha. Thanks for the chat. [Leave]
The second I do that, I'd be out of a job. Then my family would be forced to live in one of those deathtraps. And that's if we're lucky.
Hmm. Yeah. Let's talk a bit more about you.
Wow, that's awful. Let's talk about something else.
This is kind of bumming me out. I'm going to go for a walk. [Leave]
That's it? You done? Nice camera, by the way.
Thanks for doing this.
All done. Appreciate it.
Thanks for doing this.
See you later. [Leave]
Alright, are we done here now, or what?
Yeah. See you later.
No, let's talk some more.
Ah yes, grandfather steam. What about it?
Nothing. I wanted to talk about something else, actually.
Someone told me you did it.
Everyone knows it was you.
One of the hands is missing. Any idea what might have happened?
I know, kid. Just please do this, and you can take your picture.
Sure, but I wanted to talk to you about something else first.
Fine.
Is that all?
I want to ask you about something else.
Yeah, I'm outta here. See ya.
No, I wanna know more about the clock.
You think I got nothing better to do than repeat myself? I told you, it's those shitty punks. They're always getting into trouble.
Hmm. Thanks, anyways.
What do they look like?
Couldn't you just fix the clock yourself?
A hand's missing? Shit, I wish I knew, kid. I've been working all day, so your guess would be as good as mine.
I guess I'll keep asking around.
Do you think you could fix it?
Come to think of it, I did see those punk kids snickering around it earlier. I bet it's them.
Thanks, I'll look into it.
What punks?
Can't you just fix it?
I saw you found that missing hand! Good work, kid.
What can I say? I have a way with people.
No thanks to you.
Like I said, the only one I saw touching the clock is that mother and her kid.
Got it.
Where are they?
Can't you just fix it?
Hard to say. A lot of people come by. I did hear some woman whispering something to her kid about the clock, though. Might be worth looking into.
Got it.
Where did you see them?
Can't you just fix it?
Down the street, back the way you came. They've been camping out all day in front of that toy store.
Got it.
Can't you just fix it?
Ah, you'll know 'em when you see 'em. Shitty clothes, shittier attitudes. Stick out like a sore thumb in these parts.
Understood.
Can't you just fix it?
Oh yeah? Guess you're more of a gearhead than I figured. Tell you what, if ever want to change careers, you let me know.
I'll keep that in mind.
I'm good. Thanks, though.
Anything else I can do for you?
Nah, I'm good. Later, man.
Yeah, I wanted to talk to you about something...
Pickup? What? No. I just— I'm not like that. I just...I assumed you were here for work.
I'm not, I'm here for pleasure.
Why'd you assume that?
Smokes? I dunno. How old are you, kid?
What are you, my Dad?
Old enough to tell when someone's shirking work.
How old are you?

What!? That's just...that's crazy, kid. Look...I get you want to solve this thing, but if you got one person saying I did it, then me saying otherwise cancels that out. Which brings me back to innocent.
I'll get more witnesses and get back to you.
You're guilty. So guilty.
Everyone? Oh man, I knew this was a bad idea. I'm going to be ruined. Ruined!
Why'd you do it?
Service entrance is out back.
(SARCASTIC) Now that's a pretty bold pickup line.
(INVESTIGATIVE) Is that your standard greeting for my Kind?
(SOCIAL) Well, let's head back there and share a smoke, brother. Take a break from all these stuffed shirts.
Strange way to greet someone.
Who cares?
Good luck with that, kid. I've been working my ass off all day. I don't have time to steal stupid hands from stupid clocks.
[Leave]

I guess I just panicked. This is one of the last gigs I have lined up for months and I don't know if I have enough to last until things get better. Breaking that clock seemed like a good way of drumming up business.
Didn't you realize people would see you?
Not cool, man. Not cool at all.
I don't want to hear your excuses. Just give me back the part you stole.
I'm sorry, kid. This is so awful. It's just... Everyday I'm surrounded by these people who have everything. I guess I just got thinking that this might be a way to get a little something for myself.
Didn't you realize people would see you?
Get a hold of yourself.
Now it's time to give that little something back.
Alright. Here's the missing piece. Please see if you can fix it. I'm too embarrassed to go back there and do it myself.
I'll see what I can do.
You're getting off easy here. Remember that.
Pfft. Alright, fine. Here you go. But you didn't get these from me, alright?
Thanks. Another thing...
...Wait, really? Oh, shit. Nice. [Leave]
You really got an attitude, don't you, kid? Alright, here you go, but you didn't get 'em from me, alright?
Thanks. Another thing...
Flavour country, here I come. [Leave]
No offence, kid. Our Kind doesn't have business in this neighborhood unless it's... well, business.
We're not the same kind.
And what's your business, friend?
Normally I would, but the building manager's on the warpath and that's the first place she'd look.
Always the way, isn't it?
What'd you do?
We are as far as the Apes are concerned. At least until we land enough dough that we give them a reason to pretend otherwise. So, if you're not here for work what are you doing here?
Recon for the revolution.
Taking pictures. School project.
Mechanic. All kinds. You bust it, I'll fix it. Name's Lincoln. What's your line?
I'm a student. Photography major.
...Line?
What's on your mind?
About that photo...
I burned the letter like you asked.
Can I take a picture of you?
Can I take a picture of you?
Let's talk a little about you.
I don't need that picture any more, but I did get rid of the envelope for you.
Can I have some of those smokes, man?
Those geezers knocked the hand off the clock, and I can't find it. Do you have a spare?
About the clock over there...
Don't even joke about that, kid. I've seen guys disappear for saying less.
(INVESTIGATIVE) You mean, like...killed?
Sorry. I'm just here to take photos. Class project.
Good for you, kid. I mean, it might not lead to anything, but it's always nice to know you gave it a shot. No regrets. What kind of pictures you take?
I haven't decided yet.
Sad ones.
Beautiful ones.
Thanks, kid. They had a whole ton of my Kind in the store too. Maybe next year you can go as one of those.
Maybe. Let's talk a bit more about you, though.
I don't know. Let's talk about something else.
Something to consider. I'll catch you later. [Leave]
Too true. What line of work are you in, brother?
I'm a photography student at Thaddeus Rock.
I'm an artist. Photography, mostly.
...Oh, sorry. I figured you were a delivery guy or something.
I'm not.
What gave you that impression?
My mistake. What kind of line are you in, friend?
I'm a photography major at Thaddeus Rock.
I'm an artist. Photography, mostly.
Nice. Whenever you're ready, kid.
[Take picture]
Oh yeah? What's your pleasure? Paying three times the going-rate for everything? Lemme guess: you're a student.
I'm an artist. Photography, mostly.
Bingo. Photography major.
Yeah... I've been thinking and that's not really the kind of stuff I want to put out there.
Oh, it'll be very tasteful.
I was joking. I just want to an ordinary picture. Exactly like you are now.

She's trying to rush the job. Keeps threatening to bring in some general mechanics that handle her West End properties. Says they work half as cheap and works twice as fast. It's all bullshit to get me to lower my rate, but the less I see of her, the better.
How can you be sure she's bluffing?
Why don't you just tell her off?
We all are, kid. We all are.
Ain't that the truth. [Leave]
Anyway, I wanted to ask you about something.
Best way to be! Never paint yourself into a corner. I learned how to fix every type of clock this City has to offer. And even with that, work's still pretty tight.
Interesting. Mind if I ask you a few questions?
Huh. Well, good luck with that. [Leave]
See, now that I don't get. World's sad enough as it is. Who needs the reminder?
I hadn't thought about that.
My professors apparently. They want me to be more "personal". Serious.
I like to think it makes people feel less alone in their sadness.
Well, it's a good thing you met me, then! Could've gone your whole life upsetting people.
Maybe that's what I want to do.
My teachers say that's what good art does.
Why would that make you feel alone? Everyone's sad. Except for the folks who live around here. They're just cranky.
...And also the ones able to pay for art.
I like sad things.
Can't argue with that. Go where the money is, that's what I always say.
I'll keep that in mind. [Leave]
Mind if I ask you a few questions?
Well, then you picked the right major. Nothing but sorrow ahead, kid. Heh. I'm just kidding. Kinda.
Yeah, no joke. See you. [Leave]
Mind if I ask you a few questions?
Well, I guess we all have to work for somebody. But I say, do what you want until they start paying you.
I just want the diploma, man.
Yeah, well being "serious" is where the big money is.
No. I mean... I don't know. Maybe they just lose their jobs. Maybe they just get sent away for something else. It's just...it's smart to watch what you're saying. That's all.
(SARCASTIC) Hail Apes.
Hail Apes.
See that's better, but try to put a little less stink on it. Rich folks are really particular about tone. So what are you doing around here?
I'm a photographer.
I'm working on a photography project for University.
I wouldn't go that far, but that should keep you out of harm's way, at least. So what are you doing around here if you're not working?
I'm a photographer.
I'm working on a photography project for University.
Lousy geezers. I should've known. Those pests have no respects for the things that make this City great, you know?
Yeah, for sure. Give me a spare and I'll fix the clock for now.
Whatever. Hand over the, uh, hand.
Being a clock mechanic isn't very steady work. I need to keep my clients as happy as possible. Even when they're as miserable as her. But enough of my bellyaching. What line of work are you in, kid?
I'm a student. Photography major.
I'm an artist. Photography, mostly.
Hold on. I'm not saying no, but...how about we do a normal one for a start? I can see how it feels and then talk it over with the wife.
Yeah, that could work.
Sorry, assignment's due tomorrow.

The clock I'm working on is an antique. Very rare. Very expensive. The jokers she's talking about wouldn't know how to adjust the time, let alone how to fix it. But enough of my bellyaching. What kind of line are you in, kid?
I'm a Photography major at Thaddeus Rock.
I'm an artist. Photography, mostly.
Oh...you mean the kinda photos people actually pay for! And here I was, thinking you were just doing artsy crap! Lemme ask you, how do you find folks who are willing to take their clothes off?
(SOCIAL) I just approach them on the street. Usually while they're on their smoke break.
I haven't yet.
I meant beautiful in an abstract sense. Composition, lighting...that sort of thing?
Nah, kid. I'm innocent as can be. Go ahead, see what else you can drum up. I'm just going to stand here and wait for your apology.
[Leave]
Wow. You make money at that?
Maybe someday.
Actually, I pay to do it. I'm a student at the University.
Sounds like me with bowling. But I don't go 'round calling myself a bowler. So, I'm guessing you're a student then?
No, I'm a photographer. Who happens to study.
Yeah.
I'm sorry. I've just...I've just been so stressed about money lately. I swear, I'm a good person. Or at least I used to be.
I believe you. But I'm going to need that part.
Enough whining. Hand over the part.
Oh. Uh, wow. That's uh, that's really flattering, but uh, I don't really think you want someone like me.
What makes you say that?
I don't, but my audience does.
Yeah, you're probably right. [Leave]
I mean, I'm getting pretty up there in age. The old pelt's starting to go...
Look, if you're not interested, that's fine.
Hmm. Good point. [Leave]
You'd be surprised how many people are into that.
You really do. You ever think about being a detective or something? Probably pays better than this arty stuff.
Pfft. Fat chance. I'm no sellout. [Leave]
What? No. Let's talk about something else.
Oh. So, like museum stuff?
Yeah. Like museum stuff.
They have nudes in museums too.
Huh. Well, maybe that's in one of the advanced classes. No offense, kid.
Anyway, I was wondering if I could ask you a few questions.
Yeah. Well, um...thanks for the chat. [Leave]
Oh, uh, wow. That's a lot to take in.
So are you. [Wink]
You know, what? Forget it. Let's talk about something else.
Yeah, but not the good kind.
...Anyway, I was wondering if I could ask you a few questions.
Yeah. Well, um...thanks for the chat. [Leave]
Hmm. Right. Well, I'm sure there's a market for that too. People pay to go to museums, right?
Sometimes.
Not enough.
Well...there you go!
Anyway, I was wondering if I could ask you a few questions.
Yeah. Well, um...thanks for the chat. [Leave]
Well, maybe if they got different kinds of photos, more people would. You should tell them that!
Huh. Anyway, I was wondering if I could ask you a few questions?
Yeah. Well, um...thanks for the chat. [Leave]
Does that line work on people? Look, if you want to take a normal, fully-clothed picture of me, I might be okay with that. Provided you do something for me first. I need you to destroy this for me.
[Take envelope] What is it and why?
You think? I mean, my wife says stuff like that sometimes, but I thought it was just because she has to.
If you're just going to fish for compliments, I can find someone else.
Well, now you know she wasn't. So what do you say?
If anything she's holding back. Doesn't want you to get cocky.
That's fair. So long as you're enjoying it.
I'll try to keep that in mind. [Leave]
Hmm. Mind if I ask you a few questions?
No need to be ashamed, kid. School's important. Might not lead to anything, but you have to respect a guy for giving it a shot. What kind of photos you take?
I'm more of a generalist.
Sad ones.
Beautiful ones.
I mean, I appreciate you asking, but yeah. Not really my bag.
Fair enough. Mind if I ask you a few more questions. Totally unrelated.
No worries. Take care, man. [Leave]
Totally fine, man. Your body, your choice.
Wow. This is all moving pretty fast. I think I'd need to talk it over with her first, y'know? See how she feels?
Of course.
Hmm, I don't really come to this side of town often...
Thanks. I mean, maybe we could just take like a normal one in the meantime. Like in clothes? Just to see how we work together.
That's a great idea.
I'm going to have to think about that. In the meantime, do you mind if I ask you a few questions?
That's alright, I'll find someone else. [Leave]
Hmm. Fair enough. Good luck finding someone, I guess.
Actually, do you mind if I ask you a few more questions? Totally unrelated.
Thanks anyway. [Leave]
Oh, thank the Shepard! I know I'm probably being paranoid, but these building managers tend to have eyes everywhere.
Enough chat, more snap.
Time to strike a pose, pal.
You destroy that envelope for me yet?
Not yet.
Well, I'm not posing for anything 'til you've gotten rid of it.
